AHP stores steering and queued messages together in `queuedMessages`, distinguished by `PendingMessage.kind`. Steering entries use `IAgent.sendSteeringMessage` individually, bypassing Copilot's replaceable legacy-slot buffer. The host retries deferred handoff on provider progress and correlates consumption by message ID. A handoff promise that resolves false returns the message unsent because its turn ended first; the host then steers the active turn with it or, once the chat is idle, runs it as the next turn ahead of queued messages. Steering the provider still holds keeps queued work waiting; when a held handoff resolves true while the chat is idle and steering is still pending, for example because sending it failed, the host drains again. Cancellation clears every pending steering entry, including prompts handed off but not yet consumed by the SDK, without draining queued follow-ups. A client may remove handed-off steering during a turn only when the provider implements `IAgent.withdrawSteeringMessage`; Copilot then withdraws it from the SDK with `rpc.queue.withdrawMessage`, or keeps it as its own turn if the model already received it.

+The host tells the provider who authored each message it sends, so the runtime does not treat every message as the user's. `resolveAgentMessageProvenance` ([agentMessageProvenance.ts](common/agentMessageProvenance.ts)) resolves it from host-owned state only, never from message text or URI shape, and the host supplies it on the send context (`IAgentChatContext.messageProvenance`) and on `IAgent.sendSteeringMessage`. Queued messages run as ordinary turns, so they take the same path. Copilot maps it to the SDK message `source` ([copilotMessageSource.ts](node/copilot/copilotMessageSource.ts)):
+| A person's message or steering, or an artifact prompt action a person chose | `user` | omitted (the runtime's default) |
+| The kickoff of an automation run, in a session whose origin records the automation | `automation`, with the automation's resource | `automation-<resource>` |
+| An Agent Merge repair prompt | `automation`, with `vscode.agentMerge` | `automation-vscode.agentMerge` |
+| A message another agent sent with `create_session` or `send_message` | `agent`, with the sending chat (else its session) from the delegation metadata | `agent-<chat>` |
+| Any other host notification, and any agent, tool or automation message whose author the host cannot identify | `system` | `system` |

+An agent keeps one identity across its kickoff, queued and steering messages, and two agents never share one. Copilot also sets the SDK's `clientTurnId` on every message it sends with a source. The runtime echoes it on the message's `user.message` event and persists it, and `isSyntheticUserMessage` uses it to tell these messages from the runtime's own injections, which can carry the same `system` or `agent` source. Without it, the turn would lose its boundary, live and in restored history. `clientTurnId` also reaches MCP servers as `_meta["com.github.copilot/turnId"]` for those turns.

Delivered subagent user messages, including inter-agent prompts with an `agent-*` source, start their own child-chat turns even while the child is running. The provider closes the previous child turn without ending the runtime task or changing the parent turn, suppresses the initial delegated-prompt echo and hidden SDK injections, and preserves separate messages and responses during history replay, including messages that have not received a response.

`CopilotSessionLauncher` sets `mcpOAuthTokenStorage: 'in-memory'` for created, resumed, and ephemeral SDK sessions. VS Code owns durable MCP credentials through `onMcpAuthRequest`; the runtime must not consult its persistent MCP OAuth keychain store.

Codex applies Default Permissions ↔ Auto-Review changes to subsequent steps of the active turn through `turn/settings/update`. Updates are serialized per turn and retain the native turn identity captured before queuing; completion or replacement never redirects them to another turn. Pending approvals keep their original reviewer. Approval-policy and sandbox changes, including entering or leaving Full Access, remain saved for the next turn, and the picker explains this while Codex is working or awaiting input. Host-owned tools use the running turn's applied permissions rather than a deferred selection.

+Copilot opens an SDK session in the chat's permission mode when the host has the chat's configuration loaded. [CopilotSessionLauncher](node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts) asks the session for the mode after it hands over the launch's approval policy (`ICopilotSessionRuntime.resolveInitialPermissionMode`), and passes it as `permissionMode` on create, on resume, and on the create that replaces a resume with no history. The runtime applies it before the first turn or before resumed work continues, and may refuse it. [CopilotAgentSession](node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts) treats the mode as applied only when `session.permissionModeResult` is one its approval policy accepts; then the first turn does not call `permissions.setMode` again. A refused mode, or a runtime that reports no result, leaves it to the turn-start sync, which sets the mode and fails the turn if the runtime refuses. Later changes still go through `permissions.setMode`.

+A launch asks for no mode in two cases, and the session then keeps the mode the runtime restored until the turn-start sync. First, the chat's configuration is not loaded: restoring a session reads its conversation, which resumes the SDK session, before it loads the saved configuration, so the host could only ask for its default. Second, `importChat` reloads a chat another client drove (`keepsRestoredPermissionMode`). Both matter to an import, which adopts the runtime's mode into the chat's configuration (`adoptRuntimeModes`): `AgentService.importSession` restores the session before it calls `importChat`, so an unloaded session resumes through the first case and an already loaded one through the second. Asking for a mode in either would make the import adopt the host's default, including a bypass from global auto-approval that the chat never chose.

Copilot model `configSchema` advertises both `thinkingLevel` / `reasoningEffort` and, for Auto, `tier` / `autoTier`. The legacy names retain their defaults and take precedence when both spellings are supplied. The Copilot-host aliases carry the same choices without defaults. The protocol boundary projects one spelling (`thinkingLevel` / `tier`) to positively identified VS Code clients in model schemas, chat messages, and automation templates, including updates and reconnect replay, without changing authoritative state. Mobile and unmarked peers retain the full advertised schema and receive selections using `reasoningEffort` / `autoTier`, with the same legacy-key precedence as the runtime. This keeps alias handling out of shared workbench configuration and prevents schema defaults or conflicting aliases from shadowing selections authored by other clients; no additional capability is required. Tool-spawned worker seed messages use `MessageKind.Tool` in live turns and reconstructed Copilot history; explicit follow-up messages retain their supplied origin.

Live provider runtimes that react to session config subscribe to `IAgentConfigurationService.onDidSessionConfigChange` with their explicit config resource. `AgentSideEffects` does not enumerate chats or fan config values through provider hooks.
